_comment: Worked verification examples ('how we verify'). Single source of truth rendered by index.html (entries with onHome=true, using traceShort) and validation.html (all entries, using traceFull). claim/trace values are trusted site-authored HTML — never put API or user text here. Badge label values: ok=Verified, pending=Pending, nuanced=Nuanced. sourceIds feeds cite-badge.js and each id must exist in data/sources.json.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: top five roots
caseStudies.claimHome: The five most frequent roots in the Qur'an: a-l-h (God, 2,851), q-w-l (say, 1,722), k-w-n (be, 1,390), r-b-b (Lord, 980), a-m-n (believe, 879).
caseStudies.claim: a-l-h (God, 2,851), q-w-l (say, 1,722), k-w-n (be, 1,390), r-b-b (Lord, 980), a-m-n (believe, 879).
caseStudies.traceShort: Traced to the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus (Dukes 2009–2017), corpus.quran.com dictionary. Full table on Numbers.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus, Kais Dukes 2009–2017, GPL-licensed. Dictionary interface at corpus.quran.com. Full top-10 with per-root citations on Numbers and Roots. One primary source; independent triangulation possible via any Qur'anic concordance.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: Farahi's Mufradat and Niẓām
caseStudies.claimHome: Farahi's Mufradat al-Qur'an and Niẓām al-Qur'an are foundational to the coherence-based reading school.
caseStudies.claim: Hamiduddin Farahi, Mufradat al-Qur'an and Niẓām al-Qur'an. Foundational to the coherence-based reading school.
caseStudies.traceShort: Independently corroborated by Mustansir Mir's 1986 monograph on Islahi's nazm method. Full citations on Sources.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Primary: Farahi's own Mufradat al-Qur'an and Niẓām al-Qur'an. Independent secondary corroboration: Mustansir Mir, Coherence in the Qur'an: A Study of Islahi's Concept of Nazm in Tadabbur-i Qur'an (Indianapolis: American Trust Publications, 1986, ISBN 9780892590650) — a scholarly monograph devoted to showing that Islahi's nazm method, and by extension the whole coherence-based reading school, descends directly from Farahi's Mufradat and Niẓām. Two independent sources agree; upgraded from Pending. Full citations on Sources.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: y-w-m (day)
caseStudies.claimHome: Root y-w-m (day) occurs 405 times in the Leeds corpus. Widely circulated totals such as 365 or 475 count selected surface or compound forms instead; this site has not reproduced those totals.
caseStudies.claim: Root y-w-m occurs 405 times under the Leeds corpus's root annotation. Claims of 365 or 475 use different selections of surface and compound forms; they are not results reproduced by this site.
caseStudies.traceShort: Only the 405 root total is verified here. The other totals are retained as cautions about changing the unit of count, not endorsed as findings. See Numbers.
caseStudies.traceFull: Why it stays Nuanced. The 405 total is recomputed from the cited Leeds root annotations. The often-repeated 365 and 475 totals use other, usually unstated selection rules; no inspected source or reproducible procedure for them is presently in this site's evidence record. They are mentioned only to show why the unit and inclusion rule must be declared, not as verified alternatives. Detail on Numbers.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: mercy travels with forgiveness
caseStudies.claimHome: Of every root it ever shares a verse with, r-ḥ-m (mercy) appears most often beside gh-f-r (forgiveness) — together in 91 verses, far ahead of any other pairing.
caseStudies.claim: The root r-ḥ-m (mercy) co-occurs with gh-f-r (forgiveness) in 91 verses — its most frequent verse-mate by a wide margin (its next-closest partner shares 37).
caseStudies.traceShort: Counted from the bundled co-occurrence tables (Leeds v0.4); the same pairing tops the list from gh-f-r's side too. Explore on Roots.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Counted from this site's bundled verse-level co-occurrence tables (data/cooccurrence/), derived from the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus v0.4 — recomputable from the data we ship. r-ḥ-m and gh-f-r share 91 verses; r-ḥ-m's next-closest partner shares 37, and the pairing is also the top result from gh-f-r's side (91), so it is not an artefact of one root's raw frequency. The count is descriptive: it shows the two ideas are voiced together, not what any verse means. Open either root on Roots to see its co-occurrence network.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: hapax legomena
caseStudies.claim: 12,004 surface forms (out of 18,993 unique forms) occur exactly once in the Qur'an. 395 roots (out of 1,642) occur exactly once.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed directly from the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus v0.4 word-form and root tables, which are bundled in this site's own data/morphology/ files — so the claim is recomputable by anyone, from the data this site ships, without trusting us. Published on Numbers at Study depth.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: a two-source claim
caseStudies.claim: 547 roots appear only in Meccan surahs; 198 appear only in Medinan surahs.
caseStudies.traceFull: Why two sources. This claim combines the Leeds corpus (which roots occur in which surahs) with the Cairo 1924 edition's Meccan/Medinan classification. The badge cites both; click it to see the pair. A nuance rides along: a handful of surahs are classified differently in other traditions, so the boundary counts can shift by a few under other schemes — the claim on Numbers carries that note beside it.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: "this world" and "the hereafter"
caseStudies.claim: A popular claim holds that "this world" (al-dunyā) and "the hereafter" (al-ākhira) each occur exactly 115 times. At the root level the counts are not equal: d-n-w occurs 133 times and a-kh-r 250 times. The 115/115 parity holds only for particular surface forms under one counting rule.
caseStudies.traceFull: Why it stays Nuanced. The often-repeated "115 each" figure counts specific surface forms (such as the definite al-dunyā and al-ākhira) under one selection rule. At the level this site computes — the triliteral root — the counts differ: d-n-w appears 133 times and a-kh-r 250 times (a-kh-r also carries senses like "last" and "other"), both verified from the Leeds corpus and recomputable from data/roots-summary.json. We report the honest root numbers and note that a matched count depends entirely on which forms one chooses to count — the same caution the y-w-m example makes. This site does not endorse numerical-parity claims it cannot reproduce.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: corpus size
caseStudies.claim: The bundled corpus holds 77,429 word tokens across 6,236 verses, carrying 1,642 distinct triliteral roots.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Counted by scripts/build-numbers.mjs directly from the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus v0.4 morphology bundled in data/morphology/, so anyone can recount from the data this site ships. These three totals are the denominators behind every frequency and density figure on Numbers; the counting rule and its alternatives are documented on Coverage.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: root coverage
caseStudies.claim: 49,967 of 77,429 tokens (64.53%) carry a triliteral root; the rest are mostly particles, pronouns, and other function words that have no root by definition.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Measured by scripts/compute-coverage.mjs over every bundled morphology token; the full field-by-field report, including the part-of-speech breakdown of the rootless remainder, is published on Coverage. Marked Nuanced because the share depends on the corpus's annotation choices: it bounds what any root-based statistic here can describe, which is why it is worth citing at all.

caseStudies.label: ok
caseStudies.title: surah 91, mean run length 15
caseStudies.claim: Surah 91 (al-Shams) is a monorhyme: all 15 verses share one rhyme-ending key, for a mean run length of 15, the maximum possible value.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed from the Leeds Quranic Arabic Corpus by scripts/build-rhyme-map.mjs, written to data/rhyme-summary.json and data/rhyme/91.json. Rhyme regularity ranking on Patterns.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: r-h-m / gh-f-r association scores
caseStudies.claim: r-h-m (mercy) and gh-f-r (forgive) share 91 verses: PMI 3.17, Dice 0.353, LLR 302.86, gh-f-r's top partner by every measure.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/compute-association-stats.mjs, written to data/association/ (per-root files). Method note in data/association/methods.json. Panel on the root detail view.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: r-h-m network centrality
caseStudies.claim: r-h-m ranks 32nd of 1,642 roots by degree centrality, 56th by betweenness, and 53rd by eigenvector centrality, over the root co-occurrence graph.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/compute-centrality.mjs, written to data/centrality/ (per-root files). Method note in data/centrality/methods.json. Panel on the root detail view.

caseStudies.title: discursive pivots, 137 occurrences

caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-discursive-pivots.mjs, written to data/discursive-pivots.json. Full list on Patterns.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: vocabulary variety by period (TTR, MATTR, MTLD)
caseStudies.claim: Raw form TTR falls from 0.6202 (Early Meccan) to 0.3005 (Medinan) across the four Cairo 1924 revelation periods, tracking token count almost exactly; length-robust MATTR is nearly flat instead (0.8707-0.8913), and MTLD shows a smaller, less regular decline (673.77 down to 395.98, Medinan the outlier).
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-numbers.mjs using scripts/lib/lexical-diversity.mjs, written to data/numbers.json. Full table on Numbers.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: 18,408 recurring sequences
caseStudies.claim: 18,408 distinct 3-5-word sequences recur somewhere else in the Qur'an: 6,403 by root sequence and 12,005 by surface form.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Generated by scripts/build-formulas.mjs, written to data/formulas-root.json and data/formulas-surface.json. Browse every one on Formulas.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: surah 64's formulaic density beats a length-matched null
caseStudies.claim: 55.6% of surah 64's words (root stream) belong to a phrase recurring elsewhere in the Qur'an, the highest of any surah, and higher than 10,000 length-matched resamples of the whole corpus predict (p=0.0001, survives Benjamini-Hochberg at q<0.05).
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/build-formulaic-density.mjs, written to data/formulaic-density.json. Panel on the surah 64 dossier; corpus-wide ranking on Formulas.

caseStudies.label: nuanced
caseStudies.title: j-h-m dispersion: range alone understates its concentration
caseStudies.claim: j-h-m (Hellfire) occurs in 18 of 114 surahs -- moderate by plain range -- but its normalized Deviation of Proportions is 0.7989, near the top of the ranking-eligible range, because those 18 surahs are disproportionately short.
caseStudies.traceFull: Source trace. Computed by scripts/compute-dispersion.mjs, written to data/dispersion/juHm.json. Method note in data/dispersion/methods.json. Panel on the root detail view; ranking table on Numbers.
